title: FDM troubleshooting library — batch 1
usage: Each fix maps to a slicer setting key so Smart Fix can propose a specific change. Values are starting adjustments; calibrate for the printer, filament, and nozzle.

problems.name: Stringing
symptoms: Thin plastic hairs between separate parts

likely_causes.cause: Retraction distance or speed too low
Travel moves cross open areas unnecessarily
Retraction setting does not match direct-drive or Bowden extruder

fixes.note: Reduce in 5 C steps while maintaining reliable extrusion.
Direct drive: start near 0.5-1.0 mm; Bowden: start near 3-5 mm. Calibrate.
Increase until stringing reduces without grinding or skipping.
Reduces travel across open areas.
Dry according to the filament manufacturer's recommendation.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Direct-drive K1 usually needs much less retraction than Bowden printers; begin low and increase gradually.
printer_notes.bambu: Use the installed Bambu filament profile first; avoid large retraction changes before calibrating.
printer_notes.prusa: Use the Prusa material profile first; adjust retraction in small steps.

likely_causes.cause: First layer squish or adhesion is poor
Cooling fan too strong for material

fixes.note: For ABS/ASA, use an enclosure and manufacturer-recommended bed temperature.
Adds bed contact area for warping-prone parts.
Most relevant for ABS/ASA; do not eliminate cooling blindly.
Use an enclosure for ABS/ASA and other high-shrinkage materials.
Ensure the first layer is pressed onto the bed without excessive squish.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Use the K1 enclosure or a draft shield for ABS/ASA; keep the printer away from drafts.
printer_notes.bambu: Use the Bambu material preset and chamber/enclosure guidance for ABS or ASA.
printer_notes.prusa: Use Prusa's material-specific bed and enclosure recommendations.

problems.name: Layer shift
symptoms: Upper layers are offset from lower layers
Print continues after a visible jump

likely_causes.cause: Print speed or acceleration too high for the mechanism

fixes.note: Reduce speed after checking belts and mechanics.
Use conservative acceleration while diagnosing lost steps.
Check belts, pulleys, gantry, and obstructions; this is primarily a hardware check.
Recalibrate only after mechanical issues are resolved.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Inspect belts and moving components; do not increase speed to compensate for a mechanical skip.
printer_notes.bambu: Check for debris or cable drag; use Bambu's calibration tools after mechanical inspection.
printer_notes.prusa: Check belt tension and X/Y motion; Prusa documentation emphasizes mechanical causes.

likely_causes.cause: Filament diameter or flow ratio set incorrectly
Extruder tension too low or filament grinding
Moist filament or inconsistent filament diameter

fixes.note: Only after confirming the nozzle is clear and filament diameter is correct.
Increase gradually within the filament manufacturer's safe range.
Reduces demand on the hotend and extruder.
Cold-pull or replace the nozzle if cleaning does not restore flow.
Check for grinding and consistent feeding.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Check the direct-drive path and nozzle for partial clog; verify the selected filament diameter.
printer_notes.bambu: Run Bambu's flow calibration after ruling out a clog or moisture.
printer_notes.prusa: Verify filament diameter, extruder tension, and temperature before changing flow.

problems.name: Elephant foot
symptoms: First few layers are wider than the rest
Holes at the bottom are undersized

likely_causes.cause: First layer is too close to the bed
Bed temperature too high after the first layers
First-layer width or flow too high
Heavy part pressing into the first layers

fixes.note: Raise the nozzle slightly if the first layer is overly squished.
Use a lower second-layer bed temperature if the slicer supports it.
Reduce only if the first layer is consistently too wide.
Use as a last resort after fixing first-layer height.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Adjust Z offset in small increments and reprint a first-layer test.
printer_notes.bambu: Use Bambu's first-layer calibration before applying elephant-foot compensation.
printer_notes.prusa: Use Prusa's first-layer calibration and adjust live Z if needed.

problems.name: Poor bed adhesion
symptoms: First-layer lines are uneven or disconnected

likely_causes.cause: Wrong plate surface or adhesive for material

fixes.note: Clean the plate with the manufacturer-recommended method.
Move closer only if the first layer is visibly too far away.
A slower first layer improves contact and adhesion.
Use the filament manufacturer's recommended range.
Adds contact area for small-footprint parts.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Clean the K1 plate and rerun first-layer calibration before changing adhesives.
printer_notes.bambu: Use the correct Bambu plate profile and clean according to Bambu's guidance.
printer_notes.prusa: Clean the sheet and use Prusa's recommended preparation for the filament.

likely_causes.cause: Seam placement is visible or inconsistent
Pressure advance / linear advance not calibrated

fixes.note: Move the seam to a less visible edge or align it deliberately.
Tune together with retraction speed.
Reduce only if extrusion remains reliable.
Calibrate for the filament and printer.
Use after confirming over-extrusion with a calibration print.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Start with pressure-advance calibration; then tune seam and retraction.
printer_notes.bambu: Use Bambu's pressure-advance calibration and seam settings.
printer_notes.prusa: Use Prusa's linear-advance/pressure-advance guidance and seam settings.

fixes.note: Reduce outer-wall speed first.
Lower acceleration to reduce vibration.
Improves surface finish with modest time cost.
Run the printer's input-shaping calibration after checking mechanics.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Check that the printer is stable and vibration-free; then recalibrate input shaping.
printer_notes.bambu: Use Bambu's vibration-compensation calibration after checking the printer's mounting and mechanics.
printer_notes.prusa: Reduce speed/acceleration and inspect belt tension and frame stability.

likely_causes.cause: Filament diameter setting is too large

fixes.note: Use a flow calibration print to find the correct value.
Measure the filament and set the actual diameter.
Lower gradually while extrusion remains consistent.
Reduce only if the line width is above the recommended range.

printer_notes.creality_k1: Start with flow calibration and verify filament diameter.
printer_notes.bambu: Use Bambu's flow-calibration tools and filament profile.
printer_notes.prusa: Use Prusa's extrusion/flow calibration and verify filament diameter.

problems.name: Layer separation or weak layer bonding

likely_causes.cause: Print speed too high for material
Layer height too high for nozzle

fixes.note: Increase within the filament manufacturer's range.
Gives layers more time to bond.
Especially for ABS, ASA, PETG, and tall parts.
Keep below 80% of nozzle diameter.
Dry according to the filament manufacturer's instructions.

printer_notes.creality_k1: For ABS/ASA, use an enclosure and reduce part cooling.
printer_notes.bambu: Use the Bambu filament profile and chamber guidance for high-temperature materials.
printer_notes.prusa: Use Prusa's material profile and adjust temperature/speed before reducing cooling drastically.
